sense: by chance, or on the way
also: run into someone on the street

terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with the dative
terms.gloss: meet, run into; go to meet
evidence: Phaedr. 3.7.2–3: canī perpāstō … lupus forte occurrit
Traupman 94, 284: bump into s.o., alicui occurrere
terms.comment: With the dative of the person met; forte, “by chance”, makes it an accident.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 9.23.1: cum mihi … obviam vēnisset

terms.gloss: go to meet, go and meet (someone arriving)
evidence: M-O s.v. meet, pick up: obviam īre
Ter. Eun. 5.8.34: sī tē in plateā offenderō hāc post umquam, periistī (Lewis & Short s.v. offendō)
Traupman 107: run into s.o. on the street, aliquem offendō in plateā
terms.comment: To hit upon someone, often unexpectedly: domī nōn offendissem, I wouldn’t have found him at home (Ter. Eun. 4.4.5, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: cum mihi in silvā Gallīnāriā obviam vēnisset quaesīssemque quid agerēs, dīxit tē in lectō esse
phrases.english: when [Caeparius] met me in the Gallinarian Wood and I asked how you were, he told me you were in bed

phrases.latin: canī perpāstō maciē cōnfectus lupus forte occurrit
phrases.english: a wolf worn thin with hunger happened to meet a well-fed dog

phrases.latin: quam longissimē poteris obviam nōbīs prōdeās
phrases.english: come out along the road to meet us as far as you can
to run into someone on the street
